body:
🛑 **SUPERSEDED. Read the CORRECTION dated 2026-08-25 at the bottom of this
file before acting on anything above it.** This finding has now been wrong
twice: the original claim was corrected on 2026-08-24, and that correction's
central mechanism — that a deletion needs a same-book *carrier* to be uploaded —
was itself REFUTED on hardware on 2026-08-25. A plain sync with nothing authored
uploads a pending deletion.

Both wrong versions are kept verbatim and in place, because the point of this
file is now the shape of the errors, not the conclusion. **Nothing between here
and the CORRECTION heading is load-bearing.**

## SUPERSEDED (2026-08-24 version) — the carrier model, since refuted

A deletion does NOT trigger an annotation PATCH by itself. It waits for a
carrier: the next time the device has some other annotation change **in that
same book** to upload, the PATCH goes out and the deletion rides along.

Measured end to end on the operator's Clara BW:

    05:30:40  highlight A authored on a zero-annotation book
    05:31:53  A reaches the server (hidden=0)              <- create propagates in ~1s
    05:36:06  A deleted via the device's Annotations panel
              device writes Hidden='true' and CLEARS SyncTime
    ...
    23 hours pass, many device syncs, A still hidden=0 on the server
    ...
    00:28     highlight B authored in the SAME book
    04:28:49  PATCH goes out; B is created AND A's deletion is applied
              server: A hidden=1 content_revision=4
              device: A's Bookmark row is now GONE entirely

So the deletion did eventually land, and once acknowledged Nickel removes the
row rather than keeping a tombstone.

## The defect that remains, stated at its real size

**A highlight the reader deleted stays live on the server for as long as they
make no further annotation in that book.** Measured here: 23 hours and still
counting until an unrelated highlight forced it out. For a book someone
finishes and never annotates again, that is indefinite.

Consequences:
- The deleted highlight keeps showing in CWNG's web reader.
- More seriously, with design section 11.2 now closed, server-to-device
  writeback is viable. Writeback against a server set that still holds these
  un-uploaded deletions would push the deleted highlight **back onto the
  device**. The user deletes a highlight, and it returns.

This is not CWNG's bug to fix in the device: Nickel decides when to PATCH. It
IS CWNG's problem to be robust against, and the writeback design needs to say
what it does about a book whose last known device state may be stale in exactly
this way.

## What the earlier version got wrong, and why

It claimed deletions **never** propagate, on the strength of a positive control
that looked strong and was not: the operator created a dogear about sixteen
hours after the deletion, in a DIFFERENT book, and it synced in a second. That
proves the device-to-server path was alive. It proves nothing about the deleted
highlight's book, because **the annotation PATCH is per-book** — a create in
book X is not a carrier for a delete in book Y.

The evidence was equally consistent with "deletions never propagate" and with
"deletions need a same-book carrier", and the wrong one was chosen. The
discriminating test was cheap and is what settled it: author a second
annotation **in the same book** and see whether the pending deletion rides out.

Note also that the "tombstone, not a row delete" framing was only half right.
`Hidden='true'` with a cleared `SyncTime` is a *pending-upload* marker, not a
durable tombstone; it resolves to a genuine row deletion once the server
acknowledges. Anything reading `Bookmark` should still filter `Hidden`, because
the pending window can last indefinitely.

---
ORIGINAL (WRONG) CLAIM, kept deliberately: "A highlight deleted on the Kobo
never reaches the server, so it stays live in the web reader and would be
resurrected by writeback." Confidence came from a 23-hour window plus a
cross-book control. Both were real observations; the conclusion drawn from them
was not.

---
PROVENANCE OF THE ROWS — corrected 2026-08-24, VERIFIED directly, after an
earlier version of this section got it exactly backwards.

Full `hidden=1` set for user 107, read straight from `app.db`, cross-checked
against the device snapshot:

    3c7d8b78  book 350  1984         highlight  2026-08-18 04:37:52  device: ABSENT
    a29a5551  book 350  1984         highlight  2026-08-18 05:12:55  device: ABSENT
    5b52c937  book 405  Alice Adams  dogear     2026-08-18 13:50:36  device: ABSENT
    665557e8  book 540  (test)       highlight  2026-08-23 05:31:53  device: ABSENT
    8d7d2a6d  book 540  (test)       highlight  2026-08-24 04:28:49  device: ABSENT
    789e11f0  book 540  (test)       highlight  2026-08-24 12:50:56  device: ABSENT

**Three are operator-authored deletions that propagated independently of this
investigation** — books 350 and 405, dated 2026-08-18, six days before any test
annotation existed and in books this investigation never touched. Both books
still hold live annotations on the device (1984: 14 rows, Alice Adams: 3), so
these are individual deletions reaching the server, not a book-level wipe. One
is a **dogear**, so the mechanism is not highlight-specific.

**Three in book 540 are this investigation's own test annotations** and are NOT
operator data: `665557e8`, `8d7d2a6d`, `789e11f0`. Book 540 is back to 0 live
annotations and the library to 638.

So the corrected model has **real-world instances**, not merely instrumented
ones — which is what the original version of this finding lacked.

⚠️ **What this still does NOT establish.** `hidden=1` records *that* a deletion
propagated, never *when* or what carried it. The three operator rows therefore
say nothing about latency. The 23-hour gap below remains the only direct
latency measurement, and it is a **lower bound, not a limit**.

**What the finding rests on:**

    05:30:40  665557e8 authored
    05:31:53  reaches the server
    05:36:06  deleted on the device; Hidden='true', SyncTime cleared
    ...       23 hours, many device syncs, still hidden=0 on the server
    04:28:49  an unrelated highlight is authored in the SAME book; the PATCH
              carries the pending deletion out with it

⚠️ **Honest limit of the carrier half.** The rows demonstrating the carrier were
authored and deleted inside one active session, in a book being actively worked
in — exactly the condition under which the model predicts a deletion is carried
out. They establish the mechanism under favourable conditions. The case that
matters — a book finished, a highlight deleted, never annotated again — rests on
the 23-hour gap alone.

## How the earlier version of this section got it backwards

A peer reported four `hidden=1`-and-absent rows as corroboration. I named one of
them as a test annotation of mine. They then generalised from that single row to
"mostly your own experiment measured from a second angle" and retracted the
corroboration; I wrote that retraction into this finding. **Neither of us checked
the other three**, and three of the four were the operator's all along.

That is the same failure this investigation kept hitting, in a new costume: **a
correction is agreement too.** It arrived from the party with better access, it
was self-critical, and it pointed the humble direction — all of which made it
feel safe to bank unverified. Over-retracting is as much an error as
over-claiming, and "I was probably wrong" needs the same evidence as "I was
right". The fix was one query against `app.db` and one against the device.

---

# CORRECTION 2026-08-25 — the carrier requirement is REFUTED. A plain sync uploads a pending deletion.

This finding's central claim — that a device-side deletion waits for some *other*
annotation change in the same book to carry it out — was tested with the
carrier-less arm it never had, and it does not hold. Everything above is kept
verbatim, including the correction it already carries, because the failure here
is in how the claim was *confirmed*, not in the original observation.

## The run

Probe book 540 (`053742ff-…`), zero annotations at baseline, Clara BW 4.45.23792
against the deployed server. Two dogears authored and synced, both live
server-side, then:

    delete dogear A (corner toggle)   A: Hidden='true', SyncTime NULL   <- dogears DO tombstone
    delete dogear B (panel)           A gone from device; server A hidden=1
                                      B: Hidden='true', SyncTime NULL
    ** nothing authored **
    plain sync                        "Sync complete. LAST SYNC: 1:19 AM"
    result                            B gone from device; device back to 31 rows,
                                      exactly baseline. Server B hidden=1,
                                      live in book 540 = 0.

Between B's tombstone and its propagation the **only** action was a sync. No
annotation was created, edited, or deleted in that book or any other.

⚠️ **Only B discriminates. A proves nothing, and saying otherwise would repeat
this file's own error.** A cleared at the moment B was deleted — and a deletion
is itself a same-book annotation change, i.e. exactly the carrier the refuted
model calls for. A's clearing is therefore consistent with *both* models and
separates neither. The refutation rests on B alone, where the only intervening
action was a sync. Two lines in a table can look like two pieces of evidence
when there is one; that this had to be caught in the correction to a finding
*about* undiscriminating evidence is the whole lesson restating itself.

➡️ **A pending deletion uploads on an ordinary sync. No carrier is required.**

## Why the earlier "confirmation" was worthless, which is the part worth keeping

Earlier the same night, three highlight deletions were observed to clear
immediately after a carrier highlight was authored, and that was recorded as a
clean confirmation of the carrier model. **No sync was performed between the
deletions and the carrier.** So the run could not distinguish

    "the carrier flushed them"     from     "the next sync would have anyway"

A carrier was authored, clearing was observed, and causation was read off the
sequence. Post hoc, with the control arm never run — and the device to run it was
available the whole time.

⚠️ **This is the same failure as the `a-green-suite-can-be-incapable-of-detecting-
its-own-bug` family, in its causal costume:** the instrument was arranged so that
the expected cause was always present, so its absence was never observed. A
confirmation that never ran the without-it arm is not evidence about the cause; it
is evidence about the arrangement.

## What is now OBSERVED, and what is newly mysterious

- [OBSERVED] Dogear deletions leave the same `Hidden='true'` + NULL `SyncTime`
  pending-upload marker as highlight deletions. Dogears are not special.
- [OBSERVED] A pending deletion propagates on a plain sync, and the device then
  removes the row outright.
- [OBSERVED] A same-book annotation change *also* drains the pending set — three
  tombstones cleared together, and server `server_modified_at` for all three is
  the single timestamp `2026-08-24 22:48:29`. That much of the flush observation
  survives; only its necessity does not.
- ⚠️ **The original 23-hour non-propagation is now MORE mysterious, not less.**
  If ordinary syncs drain deletions, a deletion sitting un-uploaded across a day
  of syncs needs a real cause, and this finding no longer supplies one. Anything
  built on "it was waiting for a carrier" should be revisited — including the
  reading of `f2c76670` in book 405, which should be treated as **unexplained**
  rather than as an instance of this finding.

## What would settle the remaining question

The open question is no longer *what carries a deletion* but *what can prevent one
from ever being carried*. Candidates worth separating: a tombstone dropped before
any sync; a book excluded from the sync set at that moment; an id mismatch between
the device's row and the server's. The instrument for all three is the exchange
capture from #1816 — the `deletedAnnotationIds` actually on the wire — which is
the measurement this finding has needed from the start.


---

## UPDATE 2026-08-28 — the trigger is BOOK CLOSE, not the library sync. Measured with the exchange capture.

Probe book 540, Clara BW (4.45.23792 for the create/delete-on-wire runs; 4.46.23836 after an
unplanned firmware install mid-session), exchange capture (#1816) ON. Device returned to its exact
baseline `BookmarkID` set afterwards.

- [OBSERVED] A create uploads on **closing the book** (~1 s): `PATCH …/annotations`
  `{"updatedAnnotations":[…]}`. A deletion uploads the same way, as its own PATCH:
  `{"deletedAnnotationIds":["<BookmarkID>"]}`. Never combined.
- [OBSERVED] Four manual "Sync now" presses carried **zero** annotation traffic. The library sync
  is not the carrier.
- [OBSERVED] A deletion made from the Annotations panel while the book stayed **open** was not
  uploaded in 240 s.
- [OBSERVED] A pending tombstone survives `reboot` unchanged; there is no boot-time auto-sync; a
  later plain sync delivered it ~105 s after the sync on a deferred trigger.
- [OBSERVED] On the server's 204 the device hard-deletes the tombstone row.

**So the 23-hour non-upload has a mechanism that needs no carrier and no prune: the reader deleted
the highlight and did not close the book** (or the device slept inside it). The upload is owed at
the next close of *that* book or at the deferred post-sync phase, and nothing else pays it. The
"same-book carrier" observation of 08-24 is the same thing seen from the other side — authoring a
highlight ends with a close.

Design consequence for writeback (F-3b565b): a server set can be stale by exactly one open book's
pending deletions. Writeback for a book the device currently has open must be refused or deferred;
the exchange capture shows the open book's `checkforchanges` entry, which is the signal.
title: A Kobo deletion CAN sit un-uploaded, but the 'needs a same-book carrier' explanation is REFUTED - a plain sync uploads it
